nodes.name: Example III: tridiagonal ${\mathcal{S}}^\perp$, dual Newton-CG
nodes.statement: (dense, tridiagonal ${\mathcal{S}}^\perp$, dual Newton-CG): $A$ is dense SPD and ${\mathcal{S}}$ is high-dimensional but its orthogonal complement ${\mathcal{S}}^\perp$ has small dimension $m^\perp$, here taken to be tridiagonal (half-bandwidth $b=1$), so that $B^\ast$ is tridiagonal. The dual Newton method optimizes over the $m^\perp$ coordinates, while $M(x)$ stays dense.
nodes.section: B Algebraic examples and numerical illustrations

nodes.name: Example IV: block-permutation invariant
nodes.statement: ($\mathcal G$-invariant, $r$ blocks): $A$ is invariant under a group $\mathcal G$ of block permutations acting on $r$ blocks, and ${\mathcal{S}}$ is $\mathcal G$-invariant with $C$ constrained to have zero diagonal. The problem reduces to the fixed-point subspace ${\mathcal{S}}^{\mathcal G}$ of dimension $m_{\mathcal G} \le r(r+1)/2$, and the per-iteration cost becomes independent of $n$.
nodes.section: B Algebraic examples and numerical illustrations

nodes.name: Example V: banded
nodes.statement: (banded): both $A$ and ${\mathcal{S}}$ have half-bandwidth $b \ll n$, so $M(x)$ is banded along the whole optimization path, a banded Cholesky factorization suffices at every iterate, and the linear algebra itself drops to $O(nb^2)$. A band-storage variant, reported as the indented row of Table~\ref{tab:scaling_summary}, stores only the band and so reaches much larger $n$.
nodes.section: B Algebraic examples and numerical illustrations

nodes.name: Example VI: circulant
nodes.statement: (circulant): $A$ and every $D_k$ are circulant and symmetric, so $M(x)$ stays circulant along the optimization path and is diagonalized by the discrete Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Measured per-iteration scaling across structural settings
nodes.statement: Table~\ref{tab:scaling_summary} reports the measured per-iteration cost of recovering the same pair $(B^\ast,C^\ast)$ in each setting, and Figure~\ref{fig:scaling} its growth with $n$. What structure buys is best read against the naive alternative for each setting, which differs from one to the next. On the banded instance, a solver that keeps the banded factorization but drops the structure-aware Hessian and trace evaluations is slower by a factor of $6$ at $n=2{,}000$ and $20$ at $n=4{,}000$. Cost is reported per {\it Newton iteration}, the quantity Table~\ref{tab:per_iteration_complexity} bounds. For the Newton-CG settings such an iteration contains $N_{\mathrm{cg}}$ conjugate-gradient steps, a count that itself grows with $n$ in the dual example. The dual setting is the most expensive in absolute terms because it is the most demanding instance in the table: $M(x)$ is dense and the dual dimension $m^\perp=2n-1$ grows with $n$, where the dense rows keep $m$ fixed. The dual formulation is what makes it tractable, since $m\approx2\cdot10^6$ against $m^\perp=3{,}999$ at $n=2{,}000$, and Table~\ref{tab:per_iteration_complexity} puts the primal cost on the same instance roughly $330$ times higher.

nodes.statement_short: Measured costs match the bounds; structure-aware banded evaluation is 6-20x faster, and the dual is ~330x cheaper than the primal on the tridiagonal-complement instance.

nodes.name: ConstrainedDecompositionNewtonCG
nodes.statement: \caption{\textproc{ConstrainedDecompositionNewtonCG}} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \Require $A\in\mathbb{S}^n_{++}$, basis $\{D_k\}_{k=1}^m$ of ${\mathcal{S}}$ \Parameters tolerances $\texttt{tol},\texttt{tol\_cg}>0$ \Ensure The minimizer $x$, $C^\ast=C(x)$, and $B^\ast=(A-C^\ast)^{-1}$ \State $x\gets0$, \; $(\Phi,g,B)\gets\Call{EvaluatePhiGrad}{A,x}$ \While{$\|g\|_2>\texttt{tol}$} \State $d\gets0$, \; $r\gets-g$, \; $s\gets r$ \While{$\|r\|_2>\min\{\texttt{tol\_cg},\|g\|_2\}\,\|g\|_2$} \State $q\gets\Call{HvProduct}{\{D_k\},B,s}$ \State $\theta\gets\|r\|_2^2/(s^\top q)$, \; $d\gets d+\theta s$, \; $r^{+}\gets r-\theta q$ \State $s\gets r^{+}+\bigl(\|r^{+}\|_2^2/\|r\|_2^2\bigr)s$, \; $r\gets r^{+}$ \EndWhile \State Choose $t$ by feasibility-preserving Armijo backtracking, \; $x\gets x+td$ \State $(\Phi,g,B)\gets\Call{EvaluatePhiGrad}{A,x}$ \EndWhile \State $C^\ast\gets C(x)$, \; $B^\ast\gets B$ \State \Return $x$, $C^\ast$, $B^\ast$ \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Outer Newton loop from $x=0$ with inner CG on the Newton system (relative tolerance $\min\{tol_{cg},\|g\|\}$), then feasibility-preserving Armijo backtracking.
nodes.label: alg:newtoncg

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: $x\gets0$, \; $(\Phi,g,B)\gets\Call{EvaluatePhiGrad}{A,x}$

nodes.name: Newton loop
nodes.statement:
\While{$\|g\|_2>\texttt{tol}$}
 \State $d\gets0$, \; $r\gets-g$, \; $s\gets r$
 \While{$\|r\|_2>\min\{\texttt{tol\_cg},\|g\|_2\}\,\|g\|_2$}
  \State $q\gets\Call{HvProduct}{\{D_k\},B,s}$
  \State $\theta\gets\|r\|_2^2/(s^\top q)$, \; $d\gets d+\theta s$, \; $r^{+}\gets r-\theta q$
  \State $s\gets r^{+}+\bigl(\|r^{+}\|_2^2/\|r\|_2^2\bigr)s$, \; $r\gets r^{+}$
 \EndWhile
 \State Choose $t$ by feasibility-preserving Armijo backtracking, \; $x\gets x+td$
 \State $(\Phi,g,B)\gets\Call{EvaluatePhiGrad}{A,x}$
nodes.statement_short: Outer Newton loop until $\|g\|\le$ tol

nodes.name: CG init
nodes.statement: $d\gets0$, \; $r\gets-g$, \; $s\gets r$
nodes.statement_short: Initialize CG

nodes.name: CG loop
nodes.statement:
\While{$\|r\|_2>\min\{\texttt{tol\_cg},\|g\|_2\}\,\|g\|_2$}
  \State $q\gets\Call{HvProduct}{\{D_k\},B,s}$
  \State $\theta\gets\|r\|_2^2/(s^\top q)$, \; $d\gets d+\theta s$, \; $r^{+}\gets r-\theta q$
  \State $s\gets r^{+}+\bigl(\|r^{+}\|_2^2/\|r\|_2^2\bigr)s$, \; $r\gets r^{+}$
nodes.statement_short: Inner CG loop with forcing tolerance

nodes.name: Hv product
nodes.statement: $q\gets\Call{HvProduct}{\{D_k\},B,s}$
nodes.statement_short: Hessian-vector product

nodes.name: CG update
nodes.statement: $\theta\gets\|r\|_2^2/(s^\top q)$, \; $d\gets d+\theta s$, \; $r^{+}\gets r-\theta q$
nodes.statement_short: CG step length and updates

nodes.statement_short: New conjugate direction

nodes.statement: Choose $t$ by feasibility-preserving Armijo backtracking, \; $x\gets x+td$
nodes.statement_short: Backtracking line search and step

nodes.statement_short: Re-evaluate objective and gradient

nodes.name: EvaluatePhiGrad
nodes.statement: \caption{\textproc{EvaluatePhiGrad}} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \Require $A\in\mathbb{S}^n_{++}$, $x\in\Omega_x$ \Ensure $\Phi$, the gradient $g=\nabla\Phi(x)\in\mathbb{R}^m$, and $B=M^{-1}$ \State $C\gets\sum_{k=1}^m x_k D_k$, \; $M\gets A-C$ \State Factorize $M$, \; $\Phi\gets-\log\det(M)$, \; $B\gets M^{-1}$ \For{$k=1$ \textbf{to} $m$} \State $g_k\gets\mathrm{tr}(BD_k)$ \EndFor \State \Return $\Phi$, $g$, $B$ \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Factorize $M=A-C(x)$, evaluate $-\log\det M$, invert, and take the traces $\mathrm{tr}(BD_k)$.
nodes.label: alg:evaluate_phi_grad

nodes.name: Form $C$, $M$
nodes.statement: $C\gets\sum_{k=1}^m x_k D_k$, \; $M\gets A-C$

nodes.name: Factorize, $\Phi$, $B$
nodes.statement: Factorize $M$, \; $\Phi\gets-\log\det(M)$, \; $B\gets M^{-1}$

nodes.name: Loop over $k$
nodes.statement:
\For{$k=1$ \textbf{to} $m$}
 \State $g_k\gets\mathrm{tr}(BD_k)$

nodes.name: Gradient trace
nodes.statement: $g_k\gets\mathrm{tr}(BD_k)$

nodes.name: HvProduct
nodes.statement: \caption{\textproc{HvProduct}} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \Require Basis $\{D_k\}_{k=1}^m$, $B\in\mathbb{S}^n_{++}$, a vector $p\in\mathbb{R}^m$ \Ensure $q=H(x)p\in\mathbb{R}^m$ \State $D(p)\gets\sum_{\ell=1}^m p_\ell D_\ell$ \State $Y\gets B\,D(p)\,B$ \For{$k=1$ \textbf{to} $m$} \State $q_k\gets\mathrm{tr}(D_kY)$ \EndFor \State \Return $q$ \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Form $D(p)$, the two-sided product $BD(p)B$, and the traces against each $D_k$.
nodes.label: alg:hv_product

nodes.name: Form $D(p)$
nodes.statement: $D(p)\gets\sum_{\ell=1}^m p_\ell D_\ell$

nodes.name: Two-sided product
nodes.statement: $Y\gets B\,D(p)\,B$
